answer.generated: Achieving all conceptions of fairness simultaneously is difficult because different fairness criteria often conflict with each other. For example, ensuring equal treatment may lead to disparate impact, while differential treatment might violate other principles. Designers must therefore prioritize certain fairness objectives over others, trading off one notion against another. Without a clear hierarchy, no single algorithm can satisfy every fairness requirement, highlighting the inherent limitations of the machine learning paradigm in addressing complex ethical dilemmas.
